lab.name: Autonomous and Assistive Robotics
lab.department: Faculty of Engineering · Electrical Engineering and Mechatronics
lab.location: Virág Street building wing · Room V.2.08 · Debrecen, Hungary
lab.description: We develop intelligent robotic systems that navigate a changing world and extend human capabilities.
lab.about: At the University of Debrecen, A²R brings together robotics, artificial intelligence, and biomechatronics. Our researchers connect computational methods with physical platforms to investigate autonomous movement, robot cooperation, and intuitive assistive devices.

research.title: Autonomous systems
research.description: Helping robots perceive their surroundings, plan their motion, and operate in dynamic environments.

research.title: Swarm & multi-robot systems
research.description: Investigating how teams of robots coordinate through local information, distributed decisions, and shared objectives.
research.imageAlt: Small mobile robot platforms shown in the lab presentation

research.title: Assistive robotics
research.description: Developing prosthetic and rehabilitation systems around human movement, sensing, and control.
focus: Mechanical finger design and tactile sensing
research.imageAlt: Red and black bionic hand prototype developed in the lab

research.title: Human–robot interaction
research.description: Exploring how people and robots exchange information through perception, biosignals, and intuitive interfaces.
research.imageAlt: Biosignal research setup in the laboratory

projects.title: Autonomous research vehicle
projects.imageAlt: Four-wheel Ackermann steering vehicle with onboard sensors
projects.summary: A physical testbed for indoor–outdoor navigation, perception, and real-time decision-making.
projects.description: The Ackermann steering vehicle brings sensing, embedded computing, and vehicle control together on an RC-scale platform. Research explores mapping, localization, obstacle avoidance, and human-following behavior. Team work includes an RGB-D perception pipeline using Kinect v2, NVIDIA Jetson Nano, ROS 2, and TensorRT, alongside path planning and sensor fusion.

projects.title: Modular bionic hand
projects.imageAlt: Anthropomorphic bionic hand prototype with mechanical fingers
projects.summary: Reconfigurable prosthetic devices with mechanical finger designs and integrated force sensing.
projects.description: This project investigates a modular prosthetic hand with interchangeable end-effectors for different activities and user needs. Work includes anthropomorphic mechanisms, mechanical linkages for finger movement, and tactile force-sensing modules. EMG and EEG research supports the wider aim of intuitive control. The systems shown are research prototypes.

projects.title: Robotino mobile robot
projects.summary: Mobile robotics research connecting autonomous navigation, collision avoidance, and human interaction.
projects.description: Robotino supports research in mobile robot navigation and collision avoidance. The platform is used by the lab to investigate autonomous behavior in indoor environments. Elek Donát is responsible for the Robotino platform, with research interests spanning mobile robotics, navigation, and unmanned aerial vehicles.

projects.title: Aerial manipulation
projects.summary: Bringing aerial mobility and manipulation together on an experimental multirotor platform.
projects.description: The lab’s NURAI presentation documents aerial manipulation with a drone, including the physical platform and associated design work. This work connects with A²R interests in unmanned aerial vehicles, cooperative robotic systems, and control.

projects.title: Biosignals & robotic control
projects.imageAlt: Researcher wearing a biosignal headset at a computer
projects.summary: Investigating EMG, EEG, and motor imagery as interfaces between people and robotic devices.
projects.description: A²R explores biosignal processing and pattern recognition for human–robot interaction and assistive control. The supplied research presentation illustrates EEG experiments and motor imagery workflows, while the team’s research covers EMG-based control, robotic vision, and multimodal perception.

projects.title: AMR1 mobile platform
projects.imageAlt: AMR1 compact mobile robot with exposed electronics
projects.summary: A compact mobile platform within the lab’s autonomous and multi-robot research portfolio.
projects.description: AMR1 is documented in the lab’s platform portfolio. It forms part of a collection of mobile robots supporting experimental robotics and control. Contact the lab to discuss a project’s integration requirements and suitable test platforms.

projects.title: Differential delivery robot
projects.imageAlt: Small differential-drive mobile robot with sensors
projects.summary: A differential-drive research platform for mobile robotics and delivery applications.
projects.description: This mobile robot appears in the lab’s platform portfolio under autonomous differential delivery robotics. It supports the lab’s broader interest in autonomous movement, sensing, and embedded robotic systems. Platform-specific experiments and integration opportunities can be discussed with the lab.

projects.title: Service robotics & obstacle avoidance
projects.imageAlt: Service robotics & obstacle avoidance at A²R
projects.summary: Indoor service robotics connects autonomous motion with spaces shared by people.
projects.description: The Enjoy Robotics service robot supports A²R experiments in indoor movement, delivery, and interaction. The NURAI presentation documents navigation around static and moving obstacles in the lab. These demonstrations connect perception and planning with practical movement among workstations and people.

projects.title: Leader-assisted swarm localization
projects.summary: One LiDAR-equipped leader supports the localization of lower-cost follower robots.
projects.description: This proof of concept combines a leader with LiDAR and SLAM with followers using simpler onboard sensing. Markers help the leader observe followers, while estimation combines relative observations with odometry. The lab’s demonstration includes hardware and a ROS 2 / Gazebo simulation. Related research also explores decentralized localization using infrared, IMU, and Wi-Fi fusion.

projects.title: Human-following & voice-assisted robots
projects.summary: A responsive mobile robot brings together human tracking, navigation, and voice commands.
projects.description: The pet-robot project studies friendly robotic behaviour through active person following and SLAM. Team contributions span computer vision, embedded control, and offline voice interfaces with structured command execution. The video shows an early human-following demonstration in the lab.

projects.title: Robotic hand & wrist rehabilitation
projects.imageAlt: CAD animation of a related prosthetic hand mechanism
projects.summary: Mechanical devices and biosignal interfaces support research into assisted hand movement.
projects.description: The PI’s publication record documents finger rehabilitation devices, continuous passive motion for the fingers and wrist, and grounded exoskeleton mechanisms. More recent work investigates EEG and ERP interfaces for personalized stroke rehabilitation. This programme brings together mechanical design, motion control, and human intent. The displayed CAD animation illustrates related prosthetic mechanism development; it is not a clinical rehabilitation trial.

projects.title: Intelligent space & motion capture
projects.imageAlt: OptiTrack tracking visualization and the actual A²R laboratory, from the motion-capture film
projects.summary: An instrumented lab connects robot sensing, motion measurement, and spatial understanding.
projects.description: The intelligent-space research environment combines camera-based motion capture, mobile robots, and depth sensing. OptiTrack provides reference motion measurements for tracking and validation, while RGB-D and point-cloud experiments investigate how robots represent their surroundings. Calibration, synchronized measurements, and repeatable scenarios help compare navigation and control methods.

projects.title: Smart helmet: sensing & integration
projects.imageAlt: Smart helmet: sensing & integration at A²R
projects.summary: A wearable-system concept developed through architecture, mechanical design, and electronics.
projects.description: The NURAI presentation documents a smart-helmet system overview, design views, and a dedicated PCB. The project illustrates the integration of sensing and embedded electronics within a wearable form. The figures show the documented prototype-development stages.

projects.title: Muscle fatigue & movement in sport
projects.imageAlt: Muscle fatigue & movement in sport at A²R
projects.summary: EMG and inertial sensing bring laboratory measurement into dynamic sporting activity.
projects.description: A²R is developing a method to investigate muscle fatigue during tennis using EMG and IMU data. The work connects muscle activation, movement measurement, and signal analysis with biomechanics and wearable technology. The lab announced the study in May 2026. Contact the team for the current study status.

projects.title: Competition robots & autonomous challenges
projects.imageAlt: Competition robots & autonomous challenges at A²R
projects.summary: Line following, junctions, maze solving, and robot-sumo turn engineering principles into practical challenges.
projects.description: Students design, assemble, program, and refine small autonomous robots through repeated testing. The presentation includes line-following trials, competition-course footage, and maze-solving exercises. These activities develop sensing, embedded programming, control, mechanical integration, and teamwork.

facilities.title: Motion capture & validation
facilities.description: An OptiTrack camera system supports tracking of mobile robots and aerial platforms, providing a reference for navigation and control experiments.

facilities.title: Mechatronic prototyping
facilities.description: Workshop facilities connect mechanical development with electronics, enabling the team to build, adapt, and investigate physical robotic systems.

facilities.title: Assistive robotics testbed
facilities.description: Biosignal sensing and human movement experiments support the development of prosthetic and assistive robotic systems.

facilities.title: Research computing
facilities.description: Research computers support computational modeling, AI development, and the processing of robotic sensor data.

team.name: Dr. Husam A. Neamah Almusawi
team.bio: Associate Professor at the University of Debrecen and founder of A²R in 2017. He researches autonomous navigation, socially interactive robotics, biomechatronic systems, and computational modelling. He earned his MSc in Mechatronics Engineering in 2017 and PhD in Engineering Technology and Informatics in 2021, both at Debrecen, with the PhD awarded summa cum laude. Since 2025, he has also served as a Visiting Professor at Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences, teaching artificial intelligence for robotics.

team.name: Dahnial Syauqy
team.bio: A PhD researcher at the Doctoral School of Informatics and lead for the pet robot, delivery robot, and swarm projects. He holds an MSc through the joint programme of National Central University, Taiwan, and Universitas Brawijaya, Indonesia. His research covers navigation, multi-robot coordination, reinforcement learning, and machine learning on constrained devices.

team.name: Jhon Nicolas Peña Martinez
team.bio: Leads the lab’s assistive robotics area while pursuing an MSc in Mechatronics. His research develops a modular active prosthetic hand and wrist, combining mechanical design with EMG, EEG, and sensor feedback for intuitive control.

team.name: Mózes Nader
team.bio: PhD candidate at the Informatics Doctoral School, University of Debrecen, with a BSc in Electrical and Electronic Engineering and an MSc in Mechatronics Engineering. His background includes industrial, quality, and lean engineering. His research covers multimodal perception, algorithmic control, robotic vision, and biosensing.

team.name: Elek Donát
team.bio: MSc student in Mechatronics Engineering at the University of Debrecen and a TalentUD participant. His research interests include autonomous navigation, collision avoidance, mobile robotics, and unmanned aerial vehicles. He is responsible for the Robotino mobile robot.

team.name: Suliman Ahmed
team.bio: PhD student at the Informatics Doctoral School, University of Debrecen. He holds a BSc in Biomedical Engineering and an MSc in Electrical and Electronic Engineering. His interests include bionic arms, machine learning, signal processing, and remote patient monitoring systems.

team.name: Manuel Afonso Fernandes Junior
team.bio: Develops algorithms for person tracking and following. His Mechatronics Engineering work combines control theory, sensor fusion, embedded hardware, motor control, and AI perception, with particular interest in real-time performance on constrained devices.

team.name: David Pani
team.bio: Contributes to the pet-robot project, combining SLAM with active human following. His TalentUD autonomous-vehicle work includes path planning, sensor fusion, and obstacle avoidance on an RC-scale mobile platform.

team.name: Abdulrahman Mohammed Al-Allaq
team.bio: Develops a mapping robot using ROS and simultaneous localization and mapping. His background in Mechatronics Engineering includes practical robotics, three-dimensional modelling, and mechanical design.

team.name: Ali Elbishbishy
team.bio: Develops an autonomous ground vehicle with mapping and obstacle avoidance. His experience includes competitive robotics, FPV systems, integrated electrical and mechanical design, and tuning complete robotic systems.

team.name: Hassan Almakhoul
team.bio: Works on autonomous robots that follow people. He brings experience in computer vision and engineering for wind-turbine manufacturing and maintenance to his MSc research in Mechatronics.

team.name: Hamna Noor
team.bio: Investigates EMG signals and muscle-contraction detection using MATLAB and machine learning, supporting control of modular prosthetic devices. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering and has experience in embedded systems, sensors, microcontrollers, and real-time data acquisition.

team.name: Abdelrahman Islam Azmi Thabet
team.bio: Works on environments for swarm-robot experiments. A Mechatronics Engineering undergraduate, he has experience with an overprotection-system project and participation in science and IoT competitions.

team.name: Dhanuja Nawanjana Bamunusinghe
team.bio: A Mechatronics Engineering student contributing graphic design, content creation, and video editing to the lab. He combines an interest in robotics and electronics with experience in Adobe creative tools and DaVinci Resolve.

team.name: Nader Noomen
team.bio: Develops voice-assisted robotic control using offline wake-word detection, speech-to-text processing, and structured command interpretation. His technical background includes C/C++, microcontrollers, PCB design, and introductory ROS 2 development.

team.name: Meriame Ben Khalifa
team.bio: Works on mathematical modelling of autonomous robots. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Mechatronics from ISET Radès, Tunisia, and brings experience in CAD, automation, embedded systems, and programming.

team.name: Marsail Al-Baqain
team.bio: Reviews EEG sensors, their operating principles, and applications to identify challenges and opportunities for improvement. Her undergraduate Mechatronics background includes electronics, circuit analysis, programming, and practical laboratory work.

team.name: Loay Aboelenien
team.bio: Works on robotic interpretation of human hand gestures and decision-making in industrial environments. His skills include C/C++, MATLAB, PLCs, CAD, embedded hardware, automation, and measurement systems.

team.name: Sharon Uchechi Nwachukwu
team.bio: Develops the mechanical design of a modular prosthetic wrist. Her Mechanical Engineering background includes CAD modelling, assembly and drafting, manufacturing processes, engineering management, and fluid mechanics.

team.name: Abbas
team.bio: Investigates human motion as a signal of intent for navigation. The work considers trajectories, speed, body dynamics, and multimodal perception to support robots moving around people.

team.name: Ramaroson Mandrindra
team.bio: Develops the programming and electronics for a leader robot in the swarm platform. His background in Electromechanical Engineering combines programming, electronics, and mechanical systems.

team.name: Attila Csaba Gere
team.bio: Designs task-specific mechanical attachments for assistive devices. His technical training includes mechanical design, manufacturing, and automation, with competition experience in CAD and pneumatic systems.

team.name: Zaid Boudchich
team.bio: Contributes to swarm robotics with a background in Mechanical Engineering. His experience covers mechanical repairs, diagnostics, workshop maintenance, and design of replacement parts for production machinery.

team.name: Hazem Hesham
team.bio: Studies muscle activity through EMG measurements for his thesis. His work brings together EMG and IMU signals, feature extraction, and control-system research.

team.name: Hassaan Khan Sherwani
team.bio: Develops multi-node control architectures for mobile robots, including I²C communication between a master controller and subsystems. His work combines mechanical modification, embedded hardware, kinematic modelling, and real-time synchronization.

pi.title: Dr. Husam A. Neamah Almusawi
pi.subtitle: Principal Investigator · Associate Professor
pi.bio: Associate Professor at the University of Debrecen and founder of A²R in 2017. He researches autonomous navigation, socially interactive robotics, biomechatronic systems, and computational modelling. He earned his MSc in Mechatronics Engineering in 2017 and PhD in Engineering Technology and Informatics in 2021, both at Debrecen, with the PhD awarded summa cum laude. Since 2025, he has also served as a Visiting Professor at Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences, teaching artificial intelligence for robotics.
pi.research: His research connects autonomous mobile systems and human-centred robotics: navigation and obstacle avoidance, cognitive interaction, prosthetic and rehabilitation devices, optimization, and modelling. He supervises BSc, MSc, TalentUD, TDK/OTDK, and doctoral research.
pi.leadership: Vice Chair of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society Technical Committee on Control, Robotics and Mechatronics since 2023; member of IEEE IES and IEEE RAS. He contributes to international IEEE conferences and the editorial leadership of Recent Innovations in Mechatronics.

students.description: Visitors meet mobile robots, explore 3D printing, try research demonstrations, and learn how sensing connects people and machines. The lab’s outreach sessions make robotics approachable through direct experience.

guidelines.title: Code of conduct
guidelines.summary: Respect colleagues, share resources fairly, protect confidential work, and meet agreed responsibilities.
points: Treat everyone with respect and kindness.
Ask before borrowing tools or arranging visitors.
Keep workspaces organized and communicate about deadlines.

guidelines.title: General lab safety
guidelines.summary: Prepare the workspace and understand equipment before beginning an experiment.
points: Tie back long hair and keep food and drink outside.
Keep emergency stops accessible.
Disconnect power before maintenance and report hazards immediately.

guidelines.title: Soldering station
guidelines.summary: Use the soldering station only with the lab instructor’s authorization and training.
points: Inspect equipment and use the correct PPE.
Use ventilation and fume extraction; keep the iron in its stand.
Switch off, allow cooling, and clean up after work.

guidelines.title: Tools & shared equipment
guidelines.summary: Request components through the lab system and return shared resources in good condition.
points: Only authorized staff issue tools and devices.
Keep equipment in the lab unless explicitly authorized otherwise.
Tag damaged equipment and report it; do not attempt unauthorized repairs.

guidelines.title: Data & cybersecurity
guidelines.summary: Protect research data, software, and results through the lab’s approved workflows.
points: Use the official repository and approved storage.
Lock workstations, back up work, and document progress.
Obtain permission before sharing research or connecting external storage.

guidelines.title: Prusa 3D printing
guidelines.summary: Log the print, prepare the model, and follow the approved printer settings and supervision rules.
points: Check the bed, nozzle, material, and sliced file.
Monitor the first layer and follow the lab’s supervision requirements.
Remove the print safely, clean the area, and report faults.

guidelines.title: Battery charging
guidelines.summary: Use approved batteries and chargers, inspect them before use, and supervise charging under the lab’s procedures.
points: Never charge damaged, swollen, leaking, or unknown batteries.
Keep charging areas clear and follow the manufacturer’s instructions.
Report abnormal heat, smoke, or damage immediately and follow the institutional emergency plan.
